name: 12 Step
summary: Covers original 12 Step hardware, the dedicated bootloader added in firmware 1.0.0, and the newer 12 Step2 hardware with named ports.

transport._requiresSignedCrc_note: Verified against the 12 Step firmware source (12-step-firmware/firmware/Main/utils.c): crc_byte() takes `char val`, which is signed on C51, so any byte >= 0x80 sign-extends and the CRC diverges from the unsigned calculation. That file carries an explicit note that SoftStep and 12 Step do this and that QuNexus, QuNeo, BopPad, K-Mix, K-Board and KBP4 do not.
transport._usesLegacyTrailer_note: Verified against the 12 Step firmware source (12-step-firmware/firmware/MIDI/MIDI_sysex_tx.c): sendSyxFormattedMessage() encodes the payload length alone into the preamble and then emits a bare 2-byte payload CRC, with no next-length field. Receive-side only - the firmware's own receiver still expects the modern 4-byte TAIL.

notes: Applies to the modern chunked --fw-update path to a 12 Step that already has a bootloader, not the legacy pre-1.0.0 trojan-bootloader install.

The bootloader erases its whole application region when it recognizes the first firmware packet, blocking USB until that finishes, so chunk 1's reply needs several seconds' grace beyond the steady-state delay.

12 Step reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final chunk and never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards; the application-port reconnect and version check is the real success test.
Requests a reboot from the running application into bootloader mode.
Helps legacy units gain access to the dedicated bootloader flow.
Single unchunked payload, superseded by firmware_1_0_8's chunk-safe packaging.
Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging via the shared Hex_to_SysEx tool, built from 12-step-firmware's SysEx_and_Hex_Images/make_sysex_app.ps1.
Addressed with product ID 21 (0x15, the bootloader's own PID) rather than either application hardware revision's PID (20/22), so it works unmodified for both 12step1 and 12step2.
Superseded by firmware_1_0_9's boot-tare capture and revised on/off threshold defaults.
Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging via the shared Hex_to_SysEx tool, built from 12-step-firmware's SysEx_and_Hex_Images/make_sysex_app.ps1.
Addressed with product ID 21 (0x15, the bootloader's own PID) rather than either application hardware revision's PID (20/22), so it works unmodified for both 12step1 and 12step2.

Adds a 1-second boot-time tare capture for key/select sensors (margined +25%, clamped to 2/3 of the usable range) to reduce stuck-key false triggers, and raises the default on/off pressure thresholds (20/15) with an enforced off >= on/2 floor.
Preferred current 12 Step firmware image. Chunk-safe (-cs512) packaging, addressed with product ID 21 (0x15, the bootloader's own PID) so it works unmodified for both 12step1 and 12step2.

The 1.0.9 boot-tare capture no longer stops while a tether calibration mode is active, so enabling tether within the first second after boot can no longer leave a partial tare in place for the rest of the session. The tare subtraction and calibration remap are still bypassed in tether, which is what makes the calibration modes stream raw ADC.

Adds host read-back: REQUEST_PRESET takes a preset index and returns that preset's stored-length PRESET_IMAGE, REQUEST_SETTINGS returns the whole SETTINGS struct, and REQ_GLOBALS_PI returns GLOBALS plus PRESET_INFO (active preset, standalone/tether state, num_presets).

Adds LOAD_FACTORY_PRESETS (legacy type 13) and RESET_SETTINGS (legacy type 14), matching SoftStep's numbering, so a host can restore the shipped setlist or the shipped settings without erasing the serial number.

Adds REQUEST_TARE/TARE_PAYLOAD (calibration category, types 7/8): the stored boot tare after its margin and clamp, as {channel, tare} for all 29 scan slots, as the reference for a live raw-data visualizer. Tare capture is unchanged. TETHER_MIN also transmits again - its force-transmit sentinel collided with min's reset value, so on a unit resting at 0 the mode sent nothing.
